nodes.label: Toolchain: uv, ruff, mypy --strict, pytest-cov
nodes.rationale: uv for env/lock/build; ruff lint+format; mypy --strict; pytest with coverage. Matrix 3.12/3.13/3.14 because the Python floor was lowered from the scaffold's >=3.14 to >=3.12 so current-stable distros can use the library.

nodes.label: CI test job (lint, format, mypy, hermetic pytest on 3.12-3.14)
nodes.rationale: The merge gate: runs ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy src tests, and pytest -m 'not integration' with coverage on a 3.12/3.13/3.14 matrix; setup-uv overrides the repo's .python-version pin so the matrix is real.
nodes.norm_label: ci test job (lint, format, mypy, hermetic pytest on 3.12-3.14)

nodes.label: CI integration job (workflow_dispatch, continue-on-error)
nodes.rationale: Opt-in and non-blocking because it needs a model download and a live server, and a real vision model's output is not deterministic enough to gate a merge on. Installs Ollama, pulls $DESCRIBE_IT_MODEL (qwen3.5:4b), runs pytest -m integration -v -rs so skips are visible in the log.

nodes.label: Local Ollama vision inference
nodes.rationale: Alt-text at volume is cheap locally and expensive via commercial APIs; the images may be NSFW, which hosted services refuse or penalise, and a local model has no policy layer beyond its weights. 'Local' is a default not a guarantee: https:// and paths survive host normalisation so a remote Ollama behind a reverse proxy works.

nodes.label: Commercial hosted vision API (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected for per-image cost at volume and a content policy that rejects part of the corpus. Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint and llama.cpp direct are also non-goals; rationale for those not recovered.

nodes.label: stdlib urllib.request transport
nodes.rationale: The library makes three trivial JSON POSTs (/api/chat, /api/show, /api/pull). The official ollama client would add httpx + pydantic to a package whose only dependency is Pillow. Test fidelity is better: tests run against a real in-process http.server exercising the actual urllib path (404 bodies, malformed JSON, slow responses). Async is a non-goal; adescribe over asyncio.to_thread could come later.

nodes.label: ollama PyPI client (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: pulls in httpx and pydantic transitively, and mocks would replace the real HTTP path in tests.

nodes.label: In-process http.server test fixture (fake Ollama)
nodes.rationale: Records requests and returns scripted responses so 404 bodies, malformed JSON, slow handlers, NDJSON pull streams and truncated Content-Length bodies are all exercised through the real urllib code path. Lives in tests/conftest.py.

nodes.label: Minimal API contract: image in, string out, failures are exceptions
nodes.rationale: No result objects, status codes or None returns (rejected by name in spec section 1 without argument). There is no channel for partial success: anything the library will not vouch for, it raises on. describe() is sugar for Describer(**opts).describe(image, ...).
nodes.norm_label: minimal api contract: image in, string out, failures are exceptions

nodes.label: DescribeItError exception hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Shaped by what a caller would do about the failure, not where it arose. One base so 'except DescribeItError' catches everything the library raises. OllamaTimeoutError is a sibling of OllamaConnectionError, not a subclass, because a timeout usually means 'model is slow', not 'server is down'. Wrapped originals are chained via raise ... from.

nodes.label: Caller mistakes raise TypeError/ValueError, never DescribeItError
nodes.rationale: A non-image argument raises plain TypeError (the standard Python contract). Out-of-range options (max_words < 1, timeout <= 0, blank host/model, max_image_size <= 0, prompt='') raise ValueError at construction; non-int or bool max_words/max_image_size raise TypeError. Keeps 'except DescribeItError' from swallowing bugs in calling code.
nodes.norm_label: caller mistakes raise typeerror/valueerror, never describeiterror

nodes.label: qwen3.5:4b default model
nodes.rationale: Chosen at sign-off (spec Q1) on character not benchmark: Alibaba, ~3 GB, vision+thinking (thinking disabled by us); Qwen models are generally less refusal-prone than Gemma, which matters for the NSFW use case. Resolved at Describer construction, not import time, so a long-lived process does not freeze the environment it started with. Addendum: Ollama 0.32.13 on the dev machine cannot load the qwen3.5:4b blob (CLIP rope.dimension_sections error), so live tests ran with llava:7b; default unchanged.

nodes.label: gemma4:e4b (alternative model)
nodes.rationale: Reportedly higher caption quality but more likely to refuse; lost because refusal resistance is what the NSFW use case needs. Unmeasured.

nodes.label: llava:7b (model used in live runs)
nodes.rationale: Older, widely available, no thinking capability. In seven live runs it answered in English regardless of language and overran max_words in two of seven.

nodes.label: $DESCRIBE_IT_MODEL environment variable
nodes.rationale: Overrides the packaged default; read at describer construction (per call for describe()), never at import; blank counts as unset.

nodes.label: Image preparation: RGB JPEG flattened onto white
nodes.rationale: One pure function produces upload bytes: convert to RGB with alpha flattened onto white (not black: web images with transparency sit on light backgrounds and black halos mislead the model), LANCZOS thumbnail to max_size (never upscale), JPEG quality 90, base64. Happens before any socket so an unusable image fails in a millisecond. Bounds upload size and latency; models resize internally anyway.
nodes.norm_label: image preparation: rgb jpeg flattened onto white

nodes.label: EXIF orientation honoured before conversion
nodes.rationale: Phone photos are stored in sensor order with rotation in a tag, so portraits were described sideways. Applied only when orientation != 1; output carries no EXIF.

nodes.label: Wide-mode (I, I;16*, F) rescale against own min/max
nodes.rationale: Image.convert('RGB') clips 16-bit data to white, so samples are rescaled against the image's own extrema before the 8-bit conversion. I;16B/I;16L go through convert('I') first because getextrema()/point() reject them; I;16N has its bytes reinterpreted as the sys.byteorder mode because Pillow routes it through an 8-bit unpacker and clamps to 255. Do not simplify to a convert.
nodes.norm_label: wide-mode (i, i;16*, f) rescale against own min/max

nodes.label: Colour-key transparency handling
nodes.rationale: PNG colour keys arrive on RGB and L images too and were painted as the keyed colour instead of white, so any info['transparency'] is flattened onto white. A key on a wide-mode image is ignored (the key names a raw sample value and the rescale moves every sample). A key Pillow cannot apply is dropped from a copy so the caller's image keeps it.

nodes.label: Non-finite samples in F images
nodes.rationale: Normalisation is skipped in favour of Pillow's clamping conversion only when an extremum is inf. nan is rescanned because Pillow seeds its extrema scan with pixel (0,0); an all-nan image comes out black.

nodes.label: Never mutate the caller's image object
nodes.rationale: Callers who reuse an image (thumbnailing, saving) would silently get the converted, downscaled copy. Covered by enumerated test cases rather than property tests.
nodes.norm_label: never mutate the caller's image object

nodes.label: Clean the reply to a fixed point
nodes.rationale: Spec 6.1 requires clean(clean(x)) == clean(x); one layer of decoration stripping is not idempotent because models stack decoration (**"Alt text: ..."**). Removes <think> blocks (including unclosed ones), labels, balanced quotes/emphasis/code fences with info strings, collapses whitespace; empty or marker-only result is DescriptionError. Pure, so it lives in prompt.py and is table-tested without a server.
nodes.norm_label: clean the reply to a fixed point

nodes.label: BOM and zero-width characters trimmed at edges only
nodes.rationale: Interior ZWJ/ZWNJ/ZWSP are orthographically required by Persian, Urdu, Hindi, Sinhala, Malayalam, Thai and Khmer and hold emoji sequences together; a global strip corrupts them. Trimmed at leading/trailing edges of the text and of each decoration layer.
nodes.norm_label: bom and zero-width characters trimmed at edges only

nodes.label: Wrapping pairs stripped only when balanced
nodes.rationale: Interior must not contain the closing character again, so quoted text at both ends of a description survives; an apostrophe between two word characters (a child's drawing) is punctuation, not a closing quote. Fence info-string match is case-sensitive because '```Text on a wall.```' lost its first word.
nodes.norm_label: wrapping pairs stripped only when balanced

nodes.label: No sentence-level truncation of overruns
nodes.rationale: If a model overruns max_words the text is returned as-is; the caller asked for alt text, not a truncated fragment. Length is requested via the prompt, never enforced.

nodes.label: Sampling options: temperature 0.2, num_predict = max_words*4+32
nodes.rationale: Not temperature 0: a few small models degenerate into repetition at exactly 0. num_predict is a safety stop, not the length control (the prompt is): four tokens per word is well above English's ~1.3 and the constant margin keeps max_words=1 from being cut off mid-sentence. Output is therefore not reproducible run to run.

nodes.label: Private OpenerDirector per client
nodes.rationale: Both urllib module-level defaults are wrong for a localhost service, so each OllamaClient builds its own OpenerDirector with an empty ProxyHandler and no HTTPRedirectHandler. Found in unit-2 review; commit 24e3be2.

nodes.label: Ignore $http_proxy and friends
nodes.rationale: urllib's proxy support exempts nothing, not even loopback, so a machine-wide corporate proxy captured http://localhost:11434 traffic that ollama itself sends direct. Consequence: an Ollama reachable only through a proxy cannot be reached.

nodes.label: Do not follow redirects
nodes.rationale: urllib follows a 30x by rewriting a redirected POST into a body-less GET, so the image would silently not be sent. A 3xx is an OllamaResponseError naming the Location; a Location on any other status is ignored because error pages carry one too (calling a 500 a redirect would send its reader after it).

nodes.label: Explicit, opt-in model pull (ensure_model)
nodes.rationale: Pulling may download gigabytes and blocks, so it never happens implicitly: a describe call on a missing model raises ModelNotFoundError naming 'ollama pull <model>'. ensure_model() POSTs /api/pull only if /api/show reports the model missing. A model absent upstream yields an NDJSON error line on a 200 and is an OllamaResponseError, not ModelNotFoundError (reserved for 'not present on this server').

nodes.label: check() startup health check
nodes.rationale: Read-only counterpart to ensure_model: raises OllamaConnectionError if unreachable, ModelNotFoundError if absent, returns silently otherwise.

nodes.label: Hermetic unit suite as the merge gate
nodes.rationale: Most behaviour is a reaction to what a real transport produces, so client and describer tests run against an in-process http.server fixture rather than a mocked urlopen. Deterministic; needs no model, GPU or network.
nodes.norm_label: hermetic unit suite as the merge gate

nodes.label: 100% line and branch coverage gate
nodes.rationale: pragma: no cover permitted only on the __main__ guard (and the integration-skip branch). In a library this size the uncovered lines are exactly its error branches. Every new branch, including CLI argparse type functions, arrives with a test. A lower target was not weighed.

nodes.label: Opt-in, non-blocking live tests
nodes.rationale: tests/integration/test_live.py runs only with DESCRIBE_IT_INTEGRATION=1 and a host answering /api/version; the env var is checked first so collection opens no socket, and the probe uses a proxy-free opener. Never gates a merge. Seven runs with llava:7b on 2026-08-20: word-budget assertion failed 2/7, French failed 7/7; both model behaviour, assertions left as specified.

nodes.label: Structural assertions only on live output
nodes.rationale: No keyword matching because small models are not reliable enough to gate on. Length, language function words, exception type. Weak by construction, so a model that ignores an option fails them, which is information about the model.
nodes.norm_label: structural assertions only on live output

nodes.label: Property tests with hypothesis for stated invariants
nodes.rationale: Three properties: prepared image fits its bound and keeps aspect ratio; clean_response is idempotent; normalise_host always produces a usable base URL. Other invariants are covered by enumerated cases.
nodes.norm_label: property tests with hypothesis for stated invariants

nodes.label: think:false sent unconditionally
nodes.rationale: Stops thinking-capable models (qwen3.5, gemma4) burning seconds on hidden reasoning for a caption. Verified (commit b4ebab7) that Ollama 0.32 accepts the field from models that cannot think (llava:7b), so a capability probe would cost an /api/show round trip per description to learn nothing. Pinned to Ollama 0.32; a future rejection would reopen the spec's conditional. <think> blocks are still stripped belt-and-braces.

nodes.label: /api/show thinking-capability probe (rejected)
nodes.rationale: The spec's fallback if Ollama rejected think:false with a 400; the condition never arose and the probe would double the request count.

nodes.label: keep_alive omitted when unset, never sent as null
nodes.rationale: null overrides the server's own default (5 minutes) instead of asking for it, so the key is left out of the body entirely when unset.
nodes.norm_label: keep_alive omitted when unset, never sent as null

nodes.label: Host normalisation mirroring Ollama's envconfig.Host()
nodes.rationale: A scheme-less host gets http:// and, when no port is named, 11434, matching OLLAMA_HOST parsing. A host written with a scheme is used as written so http://ollama.example.com keeps meaning port 80; explicit ports and paths (Ollama under a prefix) are kept; https:// preserved for a remote Ollama behind a reverse proxy; trailing slashes removed so appending /api/chat never doubles a separator. The first implementation defaulted 11434 for URL hosts too; corrected in commit d8cf761.

nodes.label: $OLLAMA_HOST environment variable
nodes.rationale: The same variable Ollama's own CLI reads, so a machine configured for 'ollama run' needs no describe-it-specific configuration. Resolved only by Describer, never by OllamaClient: the transport reads no ambient configuration.

nodes.label: Refusal heuristic
nodes.rationale: A refusal is a valid string, and given the NSFW use case refusals are common, so the phrase list (i'm sorry, i cannot, i can't, i am unable, i'm unable, i apologise/ize, as an ai; U+2018/U+2019 apostrophes and 'i am sorry' accepted) converts 'I'm sorry, but I can't describe this image' into DescriptionRefusedError instead of garbage alt text. Documented as a heuristic; the cleaned text is on .response. Start-anchored on the cleaned text because decoration in front would defeat an anchored pattern.

nodes.label: Refusal guard (under 200 chars OR no '.' before index 60)
nodes.rationale: Fires only when a refusal phrase starts the cleaned text AND the text looks like a refusal sentence rather than a description that happens to open 'I cannot see'. OR so a long run-on refusal still fires. Accepted false positive: a short description opening with such a phrase, since the prompt forbids that opening and refusals are the common case. Dropping the heuristic was offered at sign-off (Q4) and rejected.
nodes.norm_label: refusal guard (under 200 chars or no '.' before index 60)

nodes.label: Validate configuration at construction, not first request
nodes.rationale: A bad host let through would surface later as an unrelated-looking connection error or a request sent somewhere unintended. Each value is checked by the object that uses it: host by normalise_host in OllamaClient.__init__ (credentials, query, fragment, bad scheme, unreadable port, no hostname); timeout in OllamaClient (inf is a hang with extra steps, nan loses every comparison); model and max_words in Describer. The credentials message does not quote the host back so a password cannot reach a log. Passing client= skips the host/timeout checks. The CLI converts these into usage errors (exit 2).
nodes.norm_label: validate configuration at construction, not first request

nodes.label: Layering: cli -> describer -> {image, prompt, client} -> exceptions
nodes.rationale: Two pure layers and one HTTP client under a composer; the dependency direction never reverses. config is read by cli, describer and client. Nothing is cached and nothing is global. client is the only module that opens a socket and knows nothing of PIL or prompt wording.
nodes.norm_label: layering: cli -> describer -> {image, prompt, client} -> exceptions

nodes.label: Image prepared before any socket is opened
nodes.rationale: An unusable image should cost the caller a millisecond, not a cold model load and a timeout.
nodes.norm_label: image prepared before any socket is opened

nodes.label: Environment variables: DESCRIBE_IT_MODEL, OLLAMA_HOST
nodes.rationale: Read when a describer is constructed, never at import time; blank counts as unset.

nodes.label: describe-it command line
nodes.rationale: One file prints the description alone; several print path<TAB>description per line. Failures go to stderr, the run continues, exit 1 at the end if anything failed.

nodes.label: Choosing a model
nodes.rationale: Any vision-capable tag is passed straight through. Default qwen3.5:4b for refusal resistance (unmeasured judgement); gemma4:e4b reportedly better captions but more refusals; llava:7b answered in English regardless and overran max_words in 2/7 runs.

nodes.label: Single user message, no system prompt
nodes.rationale: Several small vision models ignore or mishandle system prompts, so the built-in wording (max_words, language, optional context sentence) goes in one user message ending 'Reply with the alt text only'; the wording forbids opening with 'image of'/'picture of'/'photo of'.
nodes.norm_label: single user message, no system prompt

nodes.label: Non-goals for v0.1
nodes.rationale: Async API, streaming, batching, non-Ollama backends, result caching, automatic model pulling, guaranteed output length, vision-capability detection (Ollama returns a clear error surfaced as OllamaResponseError).

nodes.label: Three-PR stack of work units
nodes.rationale: 1 scaffold + pure layers (exceptions, image, prompt, CI); 2 client + describer + fake-server fixture; 3 CLI, integration tests, README, ARCHITECTURE, ADRs, live run recorded in the PR body.

nodes.label: Open questions Q1-Q4 and resolutions
nodes.rationale: Q1 default model -> qwen3.5:4b; Q2 GitHub -> private Xof/describe-it with PR stack and Actions CI; Q3 Python floor -> >=3.12 with 3.12/3.13/3.14 matrix; Q4 refusal strictness -> guarded heuristic.

nodes.label: Errata found during units 1-3 (2026-08-20)
nodes.rationale: Corrections discovered while implementing: fixed-point cleaning, guard rule on cleaned text, wide-mode rescale, EXIF, colour keys, non-finite samples, client= seam, validation at construction, proxy/redirect opener, host normalisation, CLI argparse types, one-line-per-file escaping, broken-pipe handling, live-test env-check order, py.typed metadata.

nodes.label: CLI one-line-per-file output contract
nodes.rationale: Every control character (C0, DEL, C1) is escaped in the description, the path and failure text, and backslashes in paths doubled, because none of the three is trusted: a tab forges a column, CR/LF split a record, ESC carries a terminal escape. clean_response is left alone since this is presentation. Failures are 'describe-it: <path>: <reason>' with whitespace collapsed. DecompressionBombWarning suppressed; each description flushed as produced.

nodes.label: Missing and closed output stream handling
nodes.rationale: With sys.stdout None there is nowhere to deliver a description, so exit 1 without work; with no stderr diagnostics are dropped. A closed pipe exits 1 quietly: both streams flushed explicitly before main returns (the interpreter's exit flush cannot handle BrokenPipeError), and only the broken stream's descriptor is pointed at /dev/null. stdout is the product, stderr is commentary.
nodes.norm_label: missing and closed output stream handling

nodes.label: Option validation via argparse type functions
nodes.rationale: Every value the library can reject is validated by an argparse type function so a bad one is a usage message and exit 2 rather than a traceback; --model and --host default to None so the env vars mean the same on the command line, and main turns the ValueError they can still raise into the same usage error.
nodes.norm_label: option validation via argparse type functions

nodes.label: client= keyword as test seam
nodes.rationale: Describer/describe() accept a ready-made OllamaClient so the suite can drive the real urllib path against an in-process server; supported public surface but not the simple-API story. Skips host/timeout validation.

hyperedges.label: One describe() call: prepare_image -> build_prompt -> OllamaClient.chat -> clean_response
DescribeItError hierarchy (nine classes shaped by what a caller would do)
Verification strategy: hermetic gate at 100% coverage plus opt-in structural live tests
